comparison: Both evaluations agree on data quality and experimental design (C1, C14, C15, C89-C91). OpenEval and peer reviewers both praise the dataset as excellent with physiologically matched time points. Note: OpenEval R1 includes additional claims (C13, C24) not addressed by peer review.

Strong disagreement on Arboretum method (C16, C35-C39). OpenEval finds the algorithm appropriately designed with reference to validation, while peer reviewers raise fundamental concerns about the constraint forcing each gene into exactly one module, noting this conflicts with expected gene pleiotropy and requesting additional statistical validation.

Disagreement on module identification and functional characterization (C17, C40-C44). OpenEval finds GO enrichment statistics highly significant and module patterns well-supported. Peer reviewers express concern that only five modules are inferred when visual inspection suggests more expression patterns exist, leaving biological interpretation murky.

Disagreement on expression conservation/divergence findings (C3, C19, C25, C29, C45-C47). OpenEval finds multiple converging lines of statistical evidence. Peer reviewers don't directly challenge correlations but express concern that discrete module classification doesn't quantify divergence well and changes could be due to small probability shifts in the algorithm.

Disagreement on temporal divergence patterns (C26, C30-C34). OpenEval finds correlation analyses across time points clearly support the claims. Peer reviewers criticize that the Arboretum approach doesn't exploit temporal details and that more than five expression patterns exist due to subtle but important temporal differences.

Disagreement on module stability metrics (C48-C50). OpenEval finds quantitative metrics with error estimates clearly document stable versus dynamic modules. Peer reviewers don't explicitly challenge findings but their concerns about discrete classification and need for assignment probability information apply to stability interpretations.

Disagreement on paralog divergence and window of opportunity (C5, C27, C56-C57, C62-C65). OpenEval finds strong statistical evidence from KS tests comparing duplicated vs non-duplicated genes. Peer reviewers' fundamental concerns about discrete module assignments and need for statistical validation of shifts undermine confidence in these paralog-specific conclusions.

Disagreement on WGD versus sporadic duplication differences (C6, C28, C58-C59, C61, C66-C68). OpenEval finds documented increased divergence and prolonged enrichment patterns with mechanistic explanation consistent with cited literature. Peer reviewers question reliability of module reassignment calls needed to distinguish these duplication types.

Disagreement on paralog fate classification (C79-C86). OpenEval finds clear quantitative classification with statistical support for enrichment patterns. Peer reviewers' concern that module changes could be due to small probability shifts directly undermines confidence in distinguishing neo-functionalization from other divergence patterns.

Disagreement on generalizability across conditions (C7, C87-C88). OpenEval finds convergence across oxidative stress and heat shock supports generality with appropriate caution. Peer reviewers' fundamental concerns about Arboretum's ability to reliably identify module reassignments apply equally to both conditions, questioning the generalization.

Disagreement on coordinated regulatory changes in metabolic transitions (C4, C20-C23, C51-C52, C60, C69-C70). OpenEval finds phylogenetic analysis supports convergent evolution with functional enrichment. Peer reviewers note genes with similar expression levels are classified into different modules, suggesting discrete assignments may not accurately reflect biological divergence.

Both evaluations express uncertainty about mechanistic claims (C53-C54, C71, C76-C78). OpenEval marks nucleosome repositioning as speculative requiring validation. Peer reviewers question biological significance of regulatory changes given concerns that the method doesn't quantify divergence well and may misclassify genes.

Both evaluations express uncertainty about Warburg Effect analogy and cancer metabolism connection (C72-C78, partial overlap). OpenEval notes the analogy lacks direct experimental validation in this system. Peer reviewers' concerns about expression quantification and module assignment reliability compound uncertainty about these mechanistic interpretations.

OpenEval evaluated background/motivation claims (C8-C12) as well-established consensus views appropriately supported by literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these introductory claims.
